body:
Fixes #111

This PR runs the JavaScript stage first in CI. Lint, `npm run test:js` and a new cross-language parity checker must pass before any Rust or C# job starts. It adds shared golden fixtures that both the Rust and C# suites must load, and it sets up the missing governance: required checks on `main`, a tracking issue for a red `Dependencies` check, contributor and agent rules, and CODEOWNERS. Following the owner's review, it also adds `@link-foundation/link-cli-server` (`js/server`), a standalone JavaScript server and embedded implementation of `clink` alongside the existing JavaScript client. The case study includes the timeline, root causes, options considered, and 27 original failed-job logs. [Case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/README.md)

### Requirements

| # | Requirement | Done by | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Rust/C# start only after the JavaScript stage succeeded for the same commit | The reusable `javascript-stage.yml` (lint, `test:js`, parity) is job `javascript` in every workflow that runs Rust or .NET: `rust`, `csharp`, `wasm`, `crash`, `ipc`, `deep-client`, `js-client`, `js-server`, `docs`, `security`, `dependencies`. Each Rust/.NET job lists it in `needs:`. A job that overrides the default success condition also requires `needs.javascript.result == 'success'`. `javascript.yml` is the entry workflow. | `workflow-policy.test.mjs`. Demonstration: commit 2c57efc5 added a failing test to `test:js` (reverted in fbf6422d). In all 11 gated workflows the stage failed at "Test JavaScript" and every Rust, .NET and WASM job was skipped, e.g. Rust [43589754262](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/43589754262) and C# [43589754138](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/43589754138); the full table is in [`ci-evidence.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/data/ci-evidence.md#gate-demonstration-requirement-1-commit-2c57efc5). |
| 2 | `test:js` out of `wasm.yml` | `test:js` runs in the JavaScript stage with Node only. `wasm.yml` keeps the WASM build and the browser tests, behind the gate. | `workflow-policy.test.mjs` |
| 3 | Parity manifest + checker, no path filter | `parity/features.json` (30 features, per-language status and test evidence, fingerprints) and `parity/check-parity.mjs`. A change to one language's sources of a feature without the others fails unless acknowledged with a reason. Path filters were removed from `rust.yml`/`csharp.yml`; `stack-paths.mjs` skips unchanged stacks inside the run, so the checks still report. | `parity/check-parity.test.mjs`, `ci-governance.test.mjs` (no `paths:` on the three required workflows) |
| 4 | Shared golden fixtures, CI fails if a suite does not load them | `parity/golden-fixtures.json` (41 fixtures). The Rust and C# golden tests write a receipt; `check-parity.mjs --receipt` fails when it is missing, short or has other hashes. The first Windows run showed that git's `core.autocrlf=true` on Windows runners rewrote the fixtures with CRLF, so `.gitattributes` marks `docs/protocol/**` as `-text`, and the checker fails if a fixture loses that attribute. | The "Check that the Rust/C# suite loaded every golden fixture" steps on all three OSes; `ci-governance.test.mjs`; `check-parity.test.mjs` (`-text` rule) |
| 5 | Document what `js/` implements vs delegates to the WASM crate | [`docs/JS-WORKBENCH.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/JS-WORKBENCH.md), linked from `docs/PARITY.md` and the README | review |
| 6 | Protection or ruleset on `main` requiring the three stage checks; `branches/main/protection` returns 200 | **Configured on the repository** (not a file): the ruleset "main requires the JavaScript, Rust and C# stages" requires `Pipeline Status (javascript)`, `(rust)` and `(csharp)`, up to date, and forbids force pushes and deletion. Classic protection forbids force pushes and deletion, so the endpoint returns 200. See "Release pushes" below. | `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/branches/main/protection` → 200; `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/rules/branches/main` lists the three checks. The initial protection setup is archived in [`branch-protection-after.json`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/data/branch-protection-after.json). |
| 7 | ~~Triage #36–#41, #49, #57; stale workflow (60 days)~~ **Reverted at the owner's request** ([comment](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/180#issuecomment-6880431278)) | The eight PRs were reopened with a comment each. No stale pull request policy exists: `stale.yml` was removed and AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING say that no pull request is closed, labelled or rebased because of age. | `ci-governance.test.mjs` fails if any workflow uses `actions/stale`, a stale setting or closes pull requests; [`ci-evidence.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/data/ci-evidence.md) records the reopening |
| 8 | Fix/close #109; red `Dependencies` on `main` opens or updates a tracking issue | #109 was already closed on 2026-10-12. Scheduled and manual audits enforce dependency freshness. On `main`, `tracking-issue` opens or updates the issue after failures and closes it after a passing enforcement audit. Ordinary pushes continue to report new upstream releases. Issue updates are serialized. The dependency refresh after merging #182 includes `cargo-audit` 0.23.0, `taiki-e/install-action` v2.90.6, `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.9.2, `lucide-react` 1.77.0 and `links-notation` 0.31.8 in Rust, WASM and the JavaScript server. | `dependency-tracking-issue.test.mjs`; a dry run against the live repository (`TRACKING_ISSUE_DRY_RUN=1`) |
| 9 | `workflows.yml`, zizmor, CodeQL, ESLint/Prettier | These were already on `main` (2026-10-24, 2026-11-06). zizmor 1.32's new `self-repository` audit flags the gate's `uses: ./.github/workflows/...`; its suggested `$/` form is rejected by actionlint (rhysd/actionlint#711, already reported, still open). The audit is disabled with that reason in `.github/zizmor.yml`, and a test forbids step-level `uses: ./` actions, which is the risk the audit targets. | actionlint and zizmor run in `Workflows` |
| 10 | `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, single-pusher rule | All three added; the single-pusher rule is in both CONTRIBUTING and AGENTS, with the exact `gh run list` command. `CLAUDE.md` includes `AGENTS.md`. | review |
| 11 | Policy test fails if a workflow can start Rust/C# without the gate | `workflow-policy.test.mjs` detects every job that installs or runs `cargo`, `rustup`, `wasm-pack`, `dotnet` or `setup-dotnet`, through `needs:` chains too. | its own tests with failing fixtures |

### Release pushes and the ruleset

The release jobs (`auto-release`/`manual-release` in `rust.yml`, `release`/`instant-release` in `csharp.yml`) push a version commit to `main`. That new commit carries no checks, so any rule that requires checks rejects it:

- Classic protection with required checks exempts only administrators, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not one.
- Making GitHub Actions a ruleset bypass actor is what the hive-mind CI/CD guide suggests. GitHub refuses it for this repository with HTTP 422 "Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization" ([evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/data/actions-bypass-422.json); `experiments/issue-111/probe-actions-bypass.sh` reproduces it).

So the ruleset's only bypass actor is deploy keys. A write deploy key was added, and its private key is the `RELEASE_DEPLOY_KEY` secret of a new `release` environment that only `main` can deploy to. The four release jobs run in that environment and check out with `ssh-key`. The C# `publish-current` dispatch on `main` keeps the recovery added by #182 and requires the JavaScript stage, lint, tests and packaging to pass. Their trusted publishing is unaffected: crates.io and NuGet check the OIDC environment claim only when a policy names an environment. `ci-governance.test.mjs` checks the four jobs. If the key is ever missing, both release scripts stop before tagging with a message that says how to restore it, and [troubleshooting](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md#a-release-push-was-declined) has the commands.

Until this PR merges, `main` still runs the old release jobs, which push with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The Rust auto-release after #182 hit GH013 at its version push. The branch fix uses the deploy key, and a rejected push now names `RELEASE_DEPLOY_KEY` in the recovery message. The first live run of the updated writer requires a merge to `main`. [Failed Rust release job](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44689293297/job/136147847955)

### How to verify

```sh
gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/branches/main/protection -i | head -1    # HTTP/2.0 200 OK
gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/rules/branches/main --jq '.[].parameters.required_status_checks[]?.context'
npm --prefix js ci && npm --prefix js run lint && npm --prefix js run test:js
node parity/check-parity.mjs --base origin/main --verbose
```

### Debugging aids

`PARITY_DEBUG` / `--verbose`, `STACK_PATHS_DEBUG`, `TRACKING_ISSUE_DEBUG`, and `TRACKING_ISSUE_DRY_RUN`. CI turns each one on when a job is re-run with debug logging. They are listed in [docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md#debug-switches).

### JavaScript server and embedded implementation

The owner's review asks for a full JavaScript server/embedded implementation next to the client. `js/server` is `@link-foundation/link-cli-server`: the Rust `clink` in plain JavaScript, with no WebAssembly or native code, for Node.js 20+, Bun and Deno on Linux, macOS and Windows ([README](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/js/server/README.md)).

- **Command line.** `bin/clink.js` accepts the Rust command-line options. The differential suite checks output, errors, and exit codes for the operations it exercises. It also reads `.lenv` and `.env` first, as the Rust one does.
- **Embedded store.** It writes the same files on disk as Rust (the `doublets` unit store, the names sidecar, the transitions and version-control logs), so either implementation opens the other's stores. The embedded API includes:
  - `NamedTypesDecorator.open` and `QueryProcessor`;
  - the decorators for transactions with crash recovery, version control, persistent transformations (triggers) and permissions, plus triplets over doublets;
  - the advisory `<db>.lock` lock interops with Rust through `flock` or `LockFileEx` on Node.js 26+ and Bun, or `Deno.FsFile.lock` on Deno.
- **File-backed `DoubletsStorage`.** `DoubletsStorage.open` / `openShared` / `openExclusive` port the Rust `DoubletsStorage<usize, FileMappedUnitStore<usize>>` over a JavaScript port of the `doublets` unit store (`unit-store*.js`, `u64` and `u32` addresses). The links are changed in place and written through on every operation, so the file is byte for byte the one Rust writes. `TransactionsDecorator` writes through it directly, as `rust/examples/embedded_store.rs` does. `examples/embedded-store/embedded-store.mjs` produces the same `db.links` as the Rust example on Node.js, Bun and Deno. A `u64` address above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` fails with `AddressOverflowError` instead of being rounded.
- **Serving.** It has the protocol server (`--serve`), the relay (`--forward`) and the client (`--connect`), over TCP and the JavaScript IPC transports, and the GraphQL endpoint for Deep (`--serve ADDR --graphql`).
- **Parity.** The feature manifest records JavaScript source and test evidence alongside Rust and C#. It records the JavaScript storage limits and the five native IPC kinds (`mq`, `sysvmq`, `mailslot`, `copydata`, `alpc`) that the server omits and the client can reach on supported platforms via its CLI bridge. JavaScript is the third suite that must load all 41 golden fixtures.

`js-server.yml` runs behind the JavaScript stage:
- the unit tests with 100 % line, branch and function coverage on Node.js, then on Bun and Deno;
- the unit tests on Linux, macOS and Windows with Node.js 20, 22 and 26;
- the embedded store example on Node.js, Bun and Deno, whose `db.links` files must be identical;
- the golden unit-store files (`test/fixtures/unit-store-*.links`, written by the Rust `unit_store_trace` driver) and a differential unit-store test that replays random operations through the Rust driver and the JavaScript store and compares every byte;
- the differential tests, which run each invocation through the Rust `clink` and through `bin/clink.js` and compare stdout, stderr, the exit status and every file written;
- the client's conformance scenarios against this package's `clink --serve` (`CLINK_JS`);
- the npm release.

Debug switches: `clink --trace`, `CLINK_IPC_TRACE=1`, `CLINK_DIFFERENTIAL_DEBUG=1`.

**Human action for the first npm release:** add this repository and `js-server.yml` as a trusted publisher of `@link-foundation/link-cli-server` on npmjs.com. The package is absent from the registry, so an npm namespace maintainer must publish the first version before configuring the trusted publisher. The pull request runs a package dry run. The release preflight on `main` prints the setup steps until npm authorization is in [REDACTED] [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/)

### Fixes found by CI

C# run [43635026592](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/43635026592) crashed its test host with `IpcException: the peer hung up`, thrown from `CloseWrite` on a System V queue. A peer that reads EOF and hangs up removes both queues, its ACK and ABORT included. A retransmitted EOF then fails with `EIDRM` (`ConnectionReset`) instead of reading the ABORT. Rust (`datagram.rs`), C# (`DatagramSession.cs`) and the JS server (`ipc-datagram.js`) now treat that failure while sending the end as a hang-up, as they already did for an ABORT. Regression tests use a link that vanishes on EOF: `a_peer_removing_the_link_before_the_end_is_acknowledged_still_ends_the_stream`, `APeerRemovingTheLinkBeforeTheEndIsAcknowledgedStillEndsTheStream`, and the matching `ipc-datagram.test.mjs` case. Each failed before the fix and passes with it. The JS client already traces and ignores send failures.

The Deno unit tests of `js-server.yml` for 5a7064a5 found that `DoubletsStorage.flush` could keep the old revision. It set the modification time to `new Date()`, which has only milliseconds. Deno 2.9 also truncates the time it is given to whole milliseconds and stores about half of all Dates one millisecond early ([`futimes-millisecond-truncation.mjs`](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/experiments/issue-111/futimes-millisecond-truncation.mjs)). The flush now asks for the middle of a millisecond later than the current modification time. The regression test 'publishes a later revision even within the millisecond of the last one' fails before the change. The Deno report contains a deterministic reproduction, workaround and proposed fix. [Deno #37212](https://github.com/denoland/deno/issues/37212)

Both findings are root causes 15 and 16 in the [case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/blob/issue-111-9490c2c7fe6e/docs/case-studies/issue-111/README.md).

### Verification on the final commit

GitHub completed all 14 workflows successfully on `12104e395a2c6ac26e04530567872e8d0d227607`, with 94 passing checks. The required JavaScript, Rust, and C# pipeline checks passed. The live `main` ruleset requires those three checks and an up-to-date branch, and the classic protection API returned HTTP 200. [PR checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/180/checks) · [Live ruleset](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/rules/27257766)

- The JavaScript stage verified the 30-feature manifest and all 41 fixture hashes. Rust and C# each verified all 41 fixtures on Linux, macOS, and Windows. [JavaScript](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856683002) · [Rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856682912) · [C#](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856683056)
- The JavaScript client and server passed cross-runtime conformance. The server also passed the Rust differential tests and npm package dry run. [JS client](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856682785) · [JS server](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856682767) · [WebAssembly](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856682781)
- Dependency enforcement and workflow lint passed. GitHub reports the two CodeQL alerts raised in review as fixed, and both inline threads are resolved. [Dependencies](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856682776) · [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856682905) · [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/actions/runs/44856682800)
title: Adopt the JavaScript-first CI gate, cross-language parity and repository governance
